questions.prompt: Which instrument has black and white keys and is played by pressing them?
questions.evidence: The keys of a piano are pressed with the fingers. A flute is blown and a tambourine is shaken.

questions.prompt: Which instrument do you shake or hit with your hand?
questions.evidence: A tambourine is a small drum with metal discs, so it is shaken or hit. The other two have strings.

questions.prompt: Sami is going to play the ______ by blowing into it.
questions.evidence: A flute is played by blowing air into it. The oud and the piano are not blown.

questions.prompt: Which of these instruments is used to play Arabian music?
questions.evidence: The oud, the mizmar, the qanun and the tabla are the Arabian instruments named in the lesson. The harp is used for western music.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Plans with am / is / are going to
questions.prompt: Lily ______ going to sing at the concert.
questions.evidence: Lily is one person, so the be verb is is: Lily is going to sing.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Plans with am / is / are going to
questions.prompt: We ______ going to play music next week.
questions.evidence: We is a plural subject, so the be verb is are: we are going to play.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Plans with am / is / are going to
questions.prompt: I ______ going to practise the piano tonight.
questions.evidence: With I the be verb is always am: I am going to practise.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Negative sentences with isn’t / aren’t going to
questions.prompt: She isn’t going to ______ to the concert.
questions.evidence: After going to the verb stays plain, so it is going to go.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Negative sentences with isn’t / aren’t going to
questions.evidence: They is plural and the sentence needs a negative be verb: they aren’t going to dance.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Questions with be going to
questions.prompt: ______ you going to play the tambourine? — Yes, I am.
questions.evidence: The answer Yes, I am shows a question with the be verb, and with you it is Are you going to …?

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Questions with be going to
questions.prompt: What ______ you going to do in the concert?
questions.evidence: The subject is you, so the be verb is are: what are you going to do?

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Time words for the future
questions.prompt: We are going to visit the theatre ______.
questions.evidence: Going to looks forward, so only tomorrow fits. Last week and yesterday are in the past.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about a concert
questions.prompt: Read the text. Which instrument does Nour play?
questions.evidence: The text says Nour plays the oud and her friend Sami plays the tabla.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about a concert
questions.prompt: In the text, the band is going to play at their school next Friday.
questions.evidence: The text says the band is going to play in a concert at their school next Friday.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about a concert
questions.prompt: In the text, Nour is going to play a long solo.
questions.evidence: The text says she is not going to play a long solo.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about a concert
questions.prompt: In the text, Nour wrote the words of the song herself.
questions.evidence: The text says she is going to sing one song and she wrote the words herself.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing sentences with be going to
questions.prompt: Make one complete sentence with these words: nour / going to / sing / one song
questions.correct: Nour is going to sing one song.
accepted: nour is going to sing one song
questions.wrongSample: Nour going to sing one song.
questions.evidence: The plan uses is going to with the subject Nour, then the plain verb sing.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing sentences with be going to
questions.prompt: Make one complete sentence with these words: they / not / going to / play / tonight
questions.correct: They aren’t going to play tonight.
accepted: they aren’t going to play tonight
they aren't going to play tonight
they are not going to play tonight
questions.wrongSample: They not going to play tonight.
questions.evidence: A negative plan uses aren’t with they, then going to and the plain verb play.
